stem: You have now examined Timmy. He is calm in his mother’s arms and in no distress, however, he looks pale. His tummy is soft, yet you can palpate a 'sausage' in his right upper quadrant. Which one of the following next steps is the LEAST urgent in Timmy’s case?

options.text: Tell the nurse and parents to keep the baby nil by mouth

explanation: Timmy’s presentation is classic for intussusception, which requires urgent surgical review, IV access, nil by mouth, and prompt imaging. A catheter urine sample is less urgent than these immediate steps.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency Medicine - Abdominal pain

rationale: Classic intussusception features are present: intermittent screaming, vomiting, pallor, 'red currant jelly' stool, and a sausage-shaped mass. Immediate priorities are to stabilise, keep NBM, gain IV access, obtain urgent imaging, and involve paediatric surgery. Urine testing is not the most urgent action.

optionExplanations.A: Useful if infection is in the differential, but it is the least urgent step here.
optionExplanations.B: Urgent surgical involvement is appropriate for suspected intussusception.
optionExplanations.C: IV access is important for fluids, analgesia, and possible resuscitation.
optionExplanations.D: Ultrasound is the preferred diagnostic test and should be arranged urgently.
optionExplanations.E: The child should be kept nil by mouth in preparation for imaging and possible intervention.

The following text applies to the questions at positions 8, 9, 10, 11, 12

Clinical Scenario 2 - Timmy

Next, you are taking a more detailed history about eight month old Timmy. He has a one day history of screaming inconsolably and poor feeding. He has also vomited breast milk twice over the past few hours. His mother has not measured any fever; there is no diarrhoea and no cold symptoms. When Timmy’s mother last changed the nappy, she noted some 'red currant jelly-like' substance. She has noted that between bouts of screaming, Timmy has been calm and at times quite sleepy.

The following five questions refer to Timmy’s clinical scenario.
